entities.name: Hans Tausen's Church
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Hans Tausen's Church (Danish: Hans Tausens Kirke) in Roskilde, Denmark, is a significant Lutheran church named for Hans Tausen (1494-1561), the Danish religious reformer known as 'the Danish Luther' — who was among the first major figures to spread Lutheran theology in Denmark and whose preaching in the early 1520s (beginning in Viborg in 1526) initiated the Danish Reformation, ultimately leading to the establishment of the Danish Lutheran state church under King Christian III in 1536 and the complete transformation of Danish religious and cultural life.

Hans Tausen's significance in Danish Reformation history parallels Luther's in Germany but with distinctive national character: a former Knight of St. John who converted to Lutheranism after possible contact with Luther himself, Tausen began preaching in Viborg in 1526 under the protection of King Frederick I. His popularity attracted thousands of listeners, created religious conflict with Catholic authorities, and demonstrated that Lutheran ideas could take root in Scandinavian soil as powerfully as in Germany. The Danish Reformation's official completion in 1536 made Denmark one of the first kingdoms to establish a state Lutheran church.

Roskilde — the historic medieval capital of Denmark and the burial place of Danish kings at Roskilde Cathedral (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) — is an appropriate location for a church honoring Tausen, as Roskilde represents the old pre-Reformation Danish ecclesiastical establishment that Tausen's movement transformed. The church named for him memorializes the Reformation's founding figure in the city that symbolizes Denmark's pre-Reformation heritage.
